method: Unit names are escaped reversibly. A-Z, a-z, 0-9, ':', '_' and '.' are kept, except a leading dot, which is written \x2e; a slash becomes '-'; every other character becomes one \xHH escape per UTF-8 byte, so 'café' is caf\xc3\xa9 and a literal hyphen is \x2d. Because '-' always stands for '/', the escape can be read back exactly. Path mode requires an absolute path: duplicate and trailing slashes and '.' components are removed, any '..' component is refused rather than simplified, the leading slash is dropped and the remaining components are joined with hyphens, so /var/lib/postgresql becomes var-lib-postgresql and the root path becomes a single '-'. A unit type suffix from the eleven types systemd-escape accepts (service, socket, device, mount, automount, swap, target, path, timer, slice, scope) is appended unescaped, or removed before decoding, and counts toward the limit. Decoding reads '-' as '/', decodes runs of \xHH as UTF-8 and prefixes '/' in path mode; it is stricter than systemd-escape and refuses raw characters that do not belong in an escaped name. Names are limited to 255 characters, NUL is refused, and malformed, non-UTF-8 or \x00 escapes are refused by name. The encoder was compared with systemd-escape from systemd 257 on 1,255 randomised and boundary inputs with no difference. Everything runs in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.

sources.title: systemd-escape(1): escapes strings for inclusion in unit names; --path normalizes an absolute path and joins its components with hyphens, and --suffix appends a unit type
systemd.unit(5): unit names may contain ASCII letters, digits, ":", "_", "." and "-", must not begin with a dot, and are limited to 255 characters
systemd.mount(5): a mount unit is named after its absolute mount point, with the path escaped into the unit name
